semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n > 1, if H_n is defined as the sum from k = 1 to n of 1 divided by k, and f_n is defined by f_n(x) equals the floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (the floor of k times x) divided by k, then for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 2, f_n of (m divided by n) is strictly less than H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for each integer n with n > 1
for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 2

payload.statement_nl: Let n > 1, define H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, and let f_n be defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, one has f_n(m/n) < H_n - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let r_k = {km/n} be the fractional part of km/n. Since floor(km/n) = km/n - r_k, we get
sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (m/n - r_k/k) = m - sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k,
so f_n(m/n) = sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k.

If m = 0, then every r_k = 0, hence f_n(0) = 0 < H_n - 1 because H_n > 1 for n > 1.

Assume m > 0 and set d = gcd(m,n). Write n = db and m = da with gcd(a,b) = 1. For k = qb + r with 0 <= q <= d - 1 and 1 <= r <= b - 1, we have r_k = {ra/b}. As r runs from 1 to b - 1, multiplication by a permutes the residues mod b, so the nonzero r_k consist of d copies of each number 1/b, 2/b, ..., (b - 1)/b. The remaining d values are 0, namely for k = b, 2b, ..., db = n.

Now order the r_k in nonincreasing order as r_1^* >= ... >= r_n^*. Then r_1^*, ..., r_n^* are exactly (b - 1)/b repeated d times, then (b - 2)/b repeated d times, and so on down to 1/b repeated d times, followed by d zeros. Since the weights 1, 1/2, ..., 1/n are decreasing, the usual exchange argument (rearrangement inequality) shows that f_n(m/n) is at most the sum obtained from this nonincreasing rearrangement. Hence
f_n(m/n) <= sum_{i=1}^n r_i^*/i = sum_{i=1}^{n-d} r_i^*/i.
For 1 <= i <= n-d, we have r_i^* = (b - ceil(i/d))/b <= 1 - i/n = (n - i)/n, because ceil(i/d) >= i/d. Therefore
f_n(m/n) <= sum_{i=1}^{n-d} (n - i)/(n i).

If d > 1, then n - d <= n - 2, so this is strictly smaller than
sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (n - i)/(n i) = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (1/i - 1/n) = H_n - 1.
If d = 1, then the rearrangement bound is exactly H_n - 1, but equality would require the original sequence (r_k) to already be nonincreasing in k. That is impossible here, because r_1 = m/n < (n - 1)/n, so the largest value (n - 1)/n is not in the first position. Thus equality cannot occur.

In all cases, f_n(m/n) < H_n - 1.
result_payload.proof_summary: Rewrite f_n(m/n) as a weighted sum of fractional parts. The fractional parts form a multiset with d copies of each j/b and d zeros, where d = gcd(m,n). Rearrangement bounds the sum by the sorted fractional parts, which yields an upper bound strictly below H_n - 1 when d > 1, and still strictly below H_n - 1 when d = 1 because the original order is not the reverse-sorted one unless m = n - 1.

used_external_facts: exchange argument / rearrangement inequality for decreasing weights
